Write down three things at work you are most thankful for this year
Say thank you, or sorry, to one colleague
lessons.noon: “I have finished the course” — Lord, right now let me run faithfully to the end, even in this small task.

lessons.title: Seated with the Lord on His Throne
lessons.theme: The overcomer’s hope is to reign together with Christ

v: Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, then I will come in to him and will dine with him, and he with me.
He who overcomes, I will give to him to sit down with me on my throne, as I also overcame and sat down with my Father on his throne.
If we endure, we will also reign with him. If we deny him, he also will deny us.

lessons.still: Knock gently three times on your desk, as if someone were at the door. Listen, and say: “Lord, I hear your voice. Today I open the door of my heart. Come in, dine with me, and go to work with me.”
teach: The church in Laodicea thought itself rich, yet did not know it was “wretched … miserable, poor, blind, and naked” (Revelation 3:17). Still the Lord did not reject them. He said: “Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, then I will come in to him and will dine with him, and he with me.” Then comes one of the most astonishing promises in Scripture: “He who overcomes, I will give to him to sit down with me on my throne, as I also overcame and sat down with my Father on his throne.”

Imagine a temporary contract worker called into the chairman’s office. He assumes his contract is ending. Instead the chairman says: “I want to give you shares in the company and a seat on the board.” Not because his numbers were the best, but because the chairman loves him. Jesus’ promise is more incredible still: not an employee pass, but a seat with him on his throne. Paul says the same: “If we endure, we will also reign with him.”

Overcoming is not about beating everyone by my own strength; it begins by opening the door and letting Jesus in to be King. The self-centred life wants to sit on the throne itself, and is crushed by power, anxiety and comparison. The self-emptied life gives the throne to Jesus, and is lifted up by him to sit with him. This is the hope of 321: to walk with each person until they become an overcomer, who will one day sit and reign with Christ. Every step of endurance at work today is not wasted.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The overcomer’s path is to let Jesus be King now, and to reign with him later. Humility means laying down power and returning to my place; when I step down from my own throne, the Lord gives me a seat on his.
lessons.scene: Meiling is raising two children on her own in Kuala Lumpur, earning her living as a freelance bookkeeper. This morning an email from her biggest client says that from next month they are switching to software and won’t need her. She sits at the dining table, the children’s school-fee bill beside her laptop, and a thought rises: “I’m such a failure.” Just then her phone lights up with a message from a sister in her small group: “Can I pray for you tonight?”
q: Who is God? — The Lord knocks at the door and promises overcomers a seat on his throne. What does that show you of his heart?
Who am I? — When work goes wrong, how do you see yourself: a failure, or someone invited by the Lord to sit with him?
How shall I respond? — If you were Meiling, how would you reply to that message, and how would you open your heart to the Lord right now?
lessons.jesus: Jesus “emptied himself, taking the form of a servant”, “becoming obedient to the point of death”, and “Therefore God also highly exalted him” (Philippians 2:7–9). His path to victory went down — humility, suffering, the cross — before it went up to the throne. He invites us to walk the same road, and promises to sit with us at its end.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for standing at my door and knocking, and never giving up on me. When I lose a client, lose a position, or feel worthless, remind me that you want me to sit with you on your throne. Today I open the door of my heart; come in and be King. Give me strength to endure, and the humility to let others pray for me. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Spend five quiet minutes opening a hidden struggle to the Lord
Let a companion pray for you, and be honest about what you need
Memorise Revelation 3:21 and repeat it when setbacks come
lessons.noon: “He who overcomes, I will give to him to sit down with me on my throne” — Lord, right now I look not at my failure but at your promise.

lessons.title: The Master’s Year-End Review
lessons.theme: Be faithful in a few things, and enter into the joy of your lord

v: “Now after a long time the lord of those servants came, and settled accounts with them.
He who received the five talents came and brought another five talents, saying, ‘Lord, you delivered to me five talents. Behold, I have gained another five talents in addition to them.’
“His lord said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.’
“He also who got the two talents came and said, ‘Lord, you delivered to me two talents. Behold, I have gained another two talents in addition to them.’
“His lord said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things. I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.’

lessons.still: Look at today’s to-do list and start with the least impressive item. Say: “Lord, this small task is also from you. Today I want to be faithful in a few things, and do them for you.”
teach: The master entrusted his property to his servants “to each according to his own ability” — five talents, two, and one. “Now after a long time the lord of those servants came, and settled accounts with them.” The one with five gained five more; the one with two gained two. Remarkably, the master says exactly the same words to both: “Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.” The master looks not at the size of the number but at faithfulness.

At the end of each year, companies hold their annual reviews: KPIs, completion rates, rankings, bonuses. The master’s settling of accounts is a kind of review too, but the criteria are very different. The servants with five and two receive identical praise, because the master asks, “Were you faithful with what I gave you?” — not, “Did you beat the others?” On God’s review form there is no trophy for first place, only one sentence: “Well done, good and faithful servant.”

The self-centred life is always comparing: he has more ability than me, she has better opportunities. Comparison makes us proud or makes us despair. The self-emptied life doesn’t ask how much others received, only: was I faithful with what the Lord entrusted to me? And the reward is not only “many things” to manage, but “Enter into the joy of your lord.” The ultimate meaning of work is not results but sharing the Lord’s joy. Change your thinking and your life changes: from living for performance to living for the master’s delight.
lessons.light: 321 Light: A shift of perspective — from the human to the divine, from the temporary to the eternal. Success is not proof, failure is not condemnation; being faithful in a few things so that Jesus receives all the glory — that is overcoming.
lessons.scene: Yongfu has fried char kway teow at a Singapore hawker centre for thirty years, starting his prep at four every morning. His son, who works at a bank, urges him to sell the stall: “Dad, you’ve worked your whole life, and it’s still just a little stall.” As he closes up today, one of the regular cleaners says, “Thank you — you always give me a bit extra.” Yongfu wipes his wok, turning his son’s words over in his mind.
q: Who is God? — The master speaks the very same words to two servants. What standard does God use to see our work?
Who am I? — Do you often compare your “ability” with others’? Does comparison make you proud, or discouraged?
How shall I respond? — If you were Yongfu, how would you answer your son, and how would you view these thirty years?
lessons.jesus: Before his public ministry, Jesus “came to Nazareth. He was subject to them”, growing up in an ordinary home, and he “increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and men” (Luke 2:51–52). Scripture calls him one “who was faithful to him who appointed him” (Hebrews 3:2). He is the best and most faithful servant, and also the master who invites us into his joy.
lessons.pray: Lord, thank you for placing me here and entrusting me with these abilities. Forgive me for so often comparing myself with others and despising the few things in my hands. Today let me be faithful in small things: preparing ingredients, keeping accounts, answering complaints, caring for my family. I don’t ask to be noticed; I only long one day to hear you say, “Well done, good and faithful servant.” In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Do the smallest task on your list as well as you can
Catch one comparison with a colleague and turn it into thanks
Thank someone who has been quietly faithful
lessons.noon: “You have been faithful over a few things” — Lord, right now I will be faithful for you in this small task in my hands.

lessons.title: The Name in the End Credits
lessons.theme: Looking back on the year, all the growth and fruit give glory to Jesus

v: Not to us, LORD, not to us, but to your name give glory, for your loving kindness, and for your truth’s sake.
Now to him who is able to do exceedingly abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that works in us,
to him be the glory in the assembly and in Christ Jesus to all generations, forever and ever. Amen.

lessons.still: Open your photo gallery and scroll back to this day a year ago. Take one look. Then close your eyes and say: “Lord, you have been here all year. Every good thing was your doing. Today I give all the glory to you.”
teach: The psalmist opens by saying it twice: “Not to us, LORD, not to us, but to your name give glory, for your loving kindness, and for your truth’s sake.” Paul praises “him who is able to do exceedingly abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that works in us”, and then says: “to him be the glory in the assembly and in Christ Jesus to all generations.” What changes us is not our effort, but the power that works within us.

When a film ends, the credits roll up line by line: director, cast, camera, lighting, crew, catering — hundreds of names. Many people have already left, but those who love film know every name had a part. Looking back over these fifty-two weeks, if you rolled the credits for your working life, you would see companions who walked with you, family who prayed, managers who reminded you, even clients who made life hard. But the name at the top, the last and the largest, is Jesus.

This year we have walked from thinking, life, daily living and relationships all the way to ministry. Perhaps you have changed a little; perhaps much weakness remains. But “he who began a good work in you will complete it” (Philippians 1:6). When the self-centred life looks back, it sees its own credit or its own failure; when the self-emptied life looks back, it sees God’s grace. The two cores: let Jesus be King; let Jesus receive all the glory. That is where our review ends.
lessons.light: 321 Light: One of the two cores — let Jesus receive all the glory. Humility is the key to revival: give credit to God and thank those around you, and everyone wins; keep the glory for yourself, and you lose your joy.
lessons.scene: Ruotong is a level designer at a games studio in Chengdu, and the project she led has just won the company’s award for best title of the year. At the ceremony the host invites her up to speak. She sees the art colleague who stayed up late with her through thirty revisions, and remembers the stretch when she nearly gave up and prayed every day. Microphone in hand, she weighs how to begin.
q: Who is God? — God is able to do “exceedingly abundantly”. Looking back on this year, where have you seen him go beyond what you asked or thought?
Who am I? — When you are praised, is your first instinct to take credit, to brush it off, or to give glory to God?
How shall I respond? — If you were Ruotong, how would you thank your colleagues in your speech while giving glory to God?
lessons.jesus: Jesus did many miracles, yet said, “I don’t seek my own glory” (John 8:50). All his life he sought the Father’s glory. He gave glory to the Father, and the Father glorified him; he emptied himself to the cross, and was therefore exalted. In him we learn that giving glory to God is not belittling ourselves, but finding our true place.
lessons.pray: God of glory, looking back on this year, I see your loving kindness and truth leading me all the way. What I thought I achieved was really your power at work in me. Forgive me for the times I took your glory, and teach me to thank the people who have walked with me. May my work and my whole life bring glory to your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Write down three things God did in your work this year
Thank someone who walked with you, and be specific
Next time you are praised, mention God’s grace
lessons.noon: “Not to us, LORD, not to us, but to your name give glory” — Lord, right now I give you all the credit for this.

lessons.title: Commissioning: Back to Work as Ambassadors
lessons.theme: Ministry stage review: examine, correct, and return to work carrying Christ’s commission

v: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.
But all things are of God, who reconciled us to himself through Jesus Christ, and gave to us the ministry of reconciliation;
namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not reckoning to them their trespasses, and having committed to us the word of reconciliation.
We are therefore ambassadors on behalf of Christ, as though God were entreating by us: we beg you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.
Jesus therefore said to them again, “Peace be to you. As the Father has sent me, even so I send you.”

lessons.still: Stand up straight, like an ambassador about to set out. Place your hand on your heart and say: “Lord, as you send me, so I will go. Tomorrow, back at my post, I am your ambassador.”
teach: Paul writes: “if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.” God not only reconciled us to himself, he “gave to us the ministry of reconciliation”. So “We are therefore ambassadors on behalf of Christ, as though God were entreating by us.” The risen Jesus said to his disciples, “As the Father has sent me, even so I send you.” A new creation is always a sent one; those who receive grace always carry grace.

When a new ambassador arrives in a host country, the first thing he does is present his credentials to the head of state, formally declaring: “I represent my nation.” From that day, every word and every appearance speaks for his country. When you return to your office, building site, ward or classroom, you go carrying the credentials of heaven. You needn’t print “minister” on your business card, but how you run meetings, treat people and face pressure all speak for your King.

Before we are sent, let us use the review and correction steps of the eight steps to look back on the ministry stage. Thinking — do I see my workplace as a harvest field God has sent me into? Life — am I living more of the self-emptied life? Daily living — do I have a regular companion and group? Relationships — have I begun walking with a spiritual child? Ministry — am I building a godly team and culture? Honestly write down one thing to correct, and open the app to complete the Workplace Health Check. Then, carrying the Lord’s peace, set out.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The aim is to build God’s order and walk with each person until they become an overcomer. 920 means living before every “2” in my life with a self-emptied “0” that bears the Spirit’s “9” fruits; 235 means companions, spiritual parents and children, and comrades. The one who is sent is an ambassador who lets Jesus be King at work.
lessons.scene: Pinyu is an engineer at a chip-design company in Hsinchu. For the past year she and two colleagues have done this course together every Wednesday lunchtime. Today is the final lesson, and the three meet on the company’s rooftop terrace to write commissioning cards for one another. Pen in hand, Pinyu wants to write the one sentence she most wants to say to her younger colleague — and the name of the person she will walk with next year.
q: Who is God? — “As the Father has sent me, even so I send you.” What does that show you about how God values you and your workplace?
Who am I? — Looking back on the ministry stage, which of thinking, life, daily living, relationships and ministry most needs review and correction?
How shall I respond? — If you were Pinyu, what would you write on the commissioning card? And whose name will you walk with next year?
lessons.jesus: Before his ascension Jesus said, “Go and make disciples of all nations”, and promised, “Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age” (Matthew 28:19–20). He sends us, yet never sends us alone. We are not ambassadors by our own strength; we return to every Monday carrying the King who is with us.
lessons.pray: Lord who sends me, thank you for making me a new creation and entrusting me with the ministry of reconciliation. Looking back on this year, I see growth and I see things that need correcting; shine your light on me and renew me. Tomorrow, as I return to my post, make me your faithful ambassador: walking with those around me, building a team that is yours, so that you are King at work and receive all the glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Complete the Workplace Health Check in the app
Write down one thing from the ministry stage to correct
Write a commissioning card for your companion
lessons.noon: “We are therefore ambassadors on behalf of Christ” — Lord, right now I return to my post carrying your peace.
